newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-BOTES KEEPS LEAD WITH SECOND 66.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-BOTES KEEPS LEAD WITH SECOND 66.

text.p: Former South African amateur matchplay champion Desvonde Botes took a two-stroke lead with a second successive 66 at the halfway stage of the Wild Coast Challenge on Friday.

The 22-year-old from Pretoria moved clear of compatriot Clinton Whitelaw and Zimbabwean Mark McNulty who were joint second on 134 after sharing the first day lead with Botes. American Tom Gillis shot a 66 to move into fourth place on 135.
South African Nic Henning, who also shared the first day lead, fell seven strokes off the pace after a 73.
Defending champion Wayne Westner of South Africa returned a second successive 70 to lie eight shots off the pace on level-par 140.
Botes, who completed steady loops of 33 and 33, said afterwards he had been confident of leading by the end of the second day.
"I'm playing well, in fact, this is the best form of my life," he said.
A swirling north-easterly wind made scoring more difficult than on the first day and McNulty, playing in the morning field, dropped shots on three holes, two of them on the more tricky back nine.
The halfway cut was made on 146 with 65 players going through to Saturday's third round.
